one_liner: Google Ads API has a documented REST/JSON interface with OAuth 2.0 and broad coverage. Production use needs developer-token or access-level approval, so it is buildable with friction.
auth_notes: REST calls send an OAuth 2.0 bearer access token, and the discovery document lists a single OAuth scope, adwords. The draft also listed a service-account flow (OTHER) and said developer tokens are optional. The supplied pages don't confirm either claim, so I dropped OTHER. The REST examples page still lists a developer token as a prerequisite.
access_notes: The supplied pages show that REST calls need OAuth credentials, test account access and a developer token. They don't describe the access-level tiers (Explorer, Basic, Standard) that the draft cited. The rubric names the Google Ads developer token as the app_review example, so I kept app_review with reduced confidence.
blocker_notes: Meaningful production use needs a developer token or access-level approval. The supplied pages don't detail the tiers. The webhook covers lead forms only. The MCP claim could not be re-verified: no supplied page supports it, and the vendor-namespace MCP registry search returned nothing.

evidence.quote: This guide contains examples of calling the REST endpoints directly, without the use of a client library.
The discovery document contains information about all the services, methods, resources and entities used in the Google Ads API
The [Authorization](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/rest/auth) guide provides instructions for generating an OAuth 2.0 access token.
See, edit, create, and delete your Google Ads accounts and data.
Prerequisites include a developer token, test account access
Use webhook to send data from Google Ads to your CRM system.
